Windows one-file release of VBA Add-in Editor. The ZIP contains `VBAAddinEditor.exe` and its SHA-256 checksum file.

## Several add-ins open at once, in tabs

Each add-in you open gets its own tab under the header, as in a browser.

- **Ctrl+Tab** / **Ctrl+Shift+Tab** (or Ctrl+PgDn / Ctrl+PgUp) switch tabs. **Ctrl+W**, Ctrl+F4 or a middle click closes one, asking first if it has unsaved changes. Drag a tab along the strip to reorder it. A dot on a tab means unsaved changes.
- Each tab keeps its own changes, undo history, recovery checkpoint, and place in every view (the module, the XML part, the cursor).
- Opening a file that is already open shows its tab. The file is read again from disk only when that tab has no unsaved changes.
- **File → Save All** (Ctrl+Alt+S) saves every tab with changes, each through its own review.
- Closing the window asks once about all tabs with unsaved changes.
- The tabs open when you close the editor open again next time. Turn this off with **File → Reopen Tabs on Start**.
- After a crash, every recovered draft is offered, not only the first.
- A save waiting for Office to let go of a file keeps waiting while you work in another tab. That tab comes to the front when it saves.
- The command box (Ctrl+K) lists the other open tabs, so you can switch to one by name.

## Copy between add-ins

Copy ribbon tabs, groups, menus and buttons, single macros, whole modules and UserForms from one add-in into another. Both add-ins can then be loaded at the same time without clashing.

- **File → Copy to Another Add-in…** copies into another open tab, or into a file it then opens in a new tab. **File → Copy from Another Add-in…** copies in from an open tab, or from a file that is only read.
- The same dialog opens from the procedure list's right-click menu (**Copy Macro to Another Add-in…**), **Module → Copy Module to Another Add-in…**, **Ribbon → Copy Controls to Another Add-in…** and the Ribbon view's right-click menu. Whatever you clicked is already ticked.
- **Drag** a procedure, a module or a ribbon control onto another add-in's tab to copy it there.
- Tick any mix of items. A ticked tab or group brings everything in it.
- Each ribbon control gets a place in the other add-in:
  - a whole tab becomes a new tab there. If that add-in has no ribbon yet, the copy gives it one.
  - a group goes on one of its tabs.
  - buttons share one new group, unless you choose one of its groups or menus.
- Everything the copied items need comes along, copied once even when several items share it:
  - the procedures they call, constants, variables, `Declare` statements, Types and Enums
  - class modules, and UserForms with their layout copied byte for byte
  - custom icons, including ones added but not yet saved. Built-in `imageMso` icons stay as they are.
- **Renaming, so both add-ins can be loaded together:** every macro Office can run by name gets the suffix, `_<other add-in's name>` by default. That covers ribbon callbacks, macros you ticked, the public argument-free Subs of a copied module, and macros run with `Application.Run`, `OnTime`, `OnKey` or `OnAction`. Modules, other public names and control ids are renamed only when the other add-in already uses them. Every reference follows the renames.
- The preview lists every addition and rename before anything changes. The copy is one Undo step in the other add-in's tab, and nothing is written until you save there.

## Tested in Excel and PowerPoint

Checked in real Excel and PowerPoint (Microsoft 365, Windows 10) on files those apps wrote themselves:

- Two copies of the same add-in were opened in two tabs. In the first, the editor added macros, a class module and a ribbon tab with two buttons (one `imageMso`, one custom picture), and saved.
- Its whole tab and three macros were copied into the second add-in, which had no ribbon, and that one was saved.
- Office then loaded **both add-ins at once**:
  - the copied macros ran under their new names, and each add-in kept its own state;
  - the name the first add-in kept still ran the first add-in's macro;
  - both tabs were on Office's ribbon, and clicking each tab's buttons ran that add-in's own macros.
- The rest of the live gate also passed: the edit/save cycle, saving while Office has the add-in loaded, and UserForm copy and edit. Only the customer file `ExistingMalformedPart.ppam` was not available.

The new automated test is `tests/integration/test_live_copy_office.py` (run with `VBAAE_LIVE_OFFICE=1`).

## Notes

- This is a development build from GitHub's Windows runner, not a qualified `-Release`.
- Copying follows calls by reading the code, not by compiling it. A macro whose name is built at run time (`Application.Run "Do" & n`) is not found. Library references are reported but not added. Sheets and names of the other add-in are never copied.
- Known bug: a module whose code starts with a blank line fails save verification ("Body mismatch"). The original file is left untouched; remove the leading blank line and save again.
